subject: NorthGate — capacity budget, token throttle & GPU lane allocation
messages:
From: John McKenna <john.mckenna@northgate.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — sizing question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to make sure we plan the right reserved capacity if we move forward — our product team is targeting a 95th percentile latency of <= 350ms for the chat endpoint (streaming allowed) and we expect bursts tied to marketing pushes. A couple of specifics:

- Typical avg prompt + response length: 60 tokens + 180 tokens = ~240 tokens per interaction.
- Expected steady-state concurrent sessions for Q4 pilot: 120–160 active users (mostly chat).
- Peak marketing burst: up to 1,800 concurrent sessions for 1–2 hours; tolerance for degraded quality under burst is limited — we'd want graceful degradation but keep core latency guarantees.

Can you give a rough token/sec capacity estimate and recommended reserved slab (GPU count/shape) and the headroom multiplier you'd recommend to be safe? Also any ops/runbook notes for warmup/cold-starts would be helpful.

Cheers,
John McKenna
Head of Platform, NorthGate AI

---

(Internal note: forwarding to Karthik's covers)

John — thanks for the detail, this is helpful. High level reply first, then I9ll drop a short spreadsheet with conservative math.

Summary (quick):
- Baseline tokens per interaction: ~240 tokens.
- Steady-state concurrency 120-160 => throughput ~ (240 tokens * 140 avg concurrent) / session-duration. If you assume ~12s average response generation (interactive chat) that maps to roughly 2,800 tokens/sec steady.
- Burst: 1,800 concurrent at same token profile => ~36,000 tokens/sec peak.

Those burst numbers are large — for typical open-models we recommend:
- Dedicated reserved slab sized to cover steady-state + 2x headroom (safety for short peaks) and a burst plan (elastic burst to shared pool) for rare marketing spikes.
- For NorthGate9s 350ms p95 target we need to bind model choice and batching policy. If you pick a 7B-ish quantized variant we can hit lower latency per-GPU for interactive lengths. If you prefer 13B for quality, expected per-GPU tokens/sec is lower and GPU count rises.

I9m looping in Ben (compute sizing) and Priyom (ops/runbook + warmup). I attached a quick calc (NG_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx) and a latency simulation plot.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm GPU equivalence assumptions used and recommend a specific slab composition (A100 vs H100 vs B float).
- Priyom: call out warmup/KV-caching recommendations and an ops playbook for marketing bursts.
- Kimberly: I9ll need a one-line on contract term impact if they request reserved GPUs + burst credits.

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

John/Karthik — did a quick pass on the worksheet, calling out assumptions up front:

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model: 13B decoder-only family (quant-e4) — chosen for quality balance.
- Per-GPU sustained throughput (online, low-latency config): ~4,500 tokens/sec for an H100-80GB equiv when using our runtime with KV cache and optimized kernels for this sequence length distribution. That number matches internal perf tests for 13B-ish at 240-token responses with modest batching.
- Steady-state throughput target: assume 140 concurrent interactions with ~12s generation => ~2,800 tokens/sec.
- Burst peak: 1,800 concurrent => ~36,000 tokens/sec.

Sizing math:
- Steady slab to sustain steady-state with 1.5x headroom: 2,800 * 1.5 = 4,200 tokens/sec => ~1 H100-equivalent GPU (4,500 t/s).
- To minimize risk and for regional redundancy, we recommend a minimum reserved slab of 3 x H100-80GB equivalents: two for steady+headroom (active) and one for redundancy/canary/maintenance. This gives ~13,500 tokens/sec reserved capacity under target latency settings.
- Burst plan: enable elastic burst credits to the hosted pool; if you want guaranteed burst capacity we model 36,000 tokens/sec / 4,500 = ~8 H100 GPUs. So full-coverage reserved approach would be 8 + redundancy = 9 GPUs.

Recommendation (practical):
- Reserved commit: 3 H100-equivalents (covers steady + ops margin + redundancy).
- Burst credits / autoscale to hosted pool for high spikes (policy: pre-warm edges via KV cache and accept slightly degraded p95 beyond burst-window).
- Headroom multiplier: factor of 3 for planning (3x steady to estimate worst-case short-term demand) but implement throttles and graceful degradation for marketing spikes.

I9ve attached a short latency sim; Priyom please sanity-check warmup timings.

-ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — sizing question (ops/runbook + final numbers)

John/Karthik/Ben/Kimberly — final ops notes and refined numbers after running a micro-sim on request patterns you gave. I prioritized latency-first configuration (p95 <= 350ms streaming).

Refined numbers: (model: 13B quant-e4; runtime: Redwood opt kernels; average response 180 tokens produced)
- Measured per-GPU effective tokens/sec (p95 latency budget): 3,800 t/s sustained when enforcing low-latency scheduling (smaller batching windows).
- Steady-state need: 140 concurrent at avg 240 tokens and 12s gen => ~2,800 t/s. With p95 buffer (x1.4) => target steady slab capacity = 3,920 t/s. That maps to ~1.1 H100-equivalents.
- Operational reserve: we suggest 2 active H100-equivalents + 1 hot standby in same region (3 reserved) — aligns with Ben9s recommendation but justified by p95 buffer and expected autoscale cold-start risk. Total reserved tokens/sec ~11,400 t/s.
- Burst coverage full-reserve (rare marketing spike) => 36,000 t/s target -> ~9.5 GPUs at 3,800 t/s each. Round-up => 10 GPUs for full coverage if NorthGate wants guaranteed latency during bursts.

Warmup & KV-cache playbook (short):
- Pre-warm strategy: during scheduled campaigns, send deterministic prefix warming traffic (2-4k tokens/sec) to ensure KV caches populate; this reduces cold-start amplification by ~40% in our tests.
- Gradual throttle policy: when autoscale to hosted pool starts, apply a soft throttle to non-authenticated heavy paths (e.g., long-context retrievals) to prioritize core chat flows.
- Canary + rollback: deploy new model variants to canary GPU(s) and measure drift on prompt set; have auto-fallback policy to smaller-quantized variant if latency regresses.

Contract / commercial note: if you choose reserved 3 GPUs + burst credits, pricing is materially lower than full 10-GPU reservation and gives similar experience most of the time. Kimberly, happy to sync for exact T&Cs.

Next steps:
- Karthik: propose MAP with 3-reserved + burst credits option + optional add-on full-reserve (10 GPUs) for guaranteed burst coverage.
- John: confirm whether you want full-reserve guarantee for marketing windows or prefer the burst-credit model.

Thanks — attached updated worksheet (NG_capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx) and MAP draft (mutual_action_plan_NG.pdf).

— Priyom Das
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
